principles: One queue, one approval moment per week. Leaders review in 15 minutes, not in scattered texts.
Every number has a source. Every public asset carries the brokerage line. Every listing hits the MLS before it hits social.
Reuse before create: one blog post becomes 4-6 assets across channels.
No new paid tools in the first 90 days. Get more out of Brivity, Fello, Canva and KW Command first.

weeklyRhythm.name: Plan
steps: Pull the newest public market data and refresh the stat cards
Confirm the week's calendar slots and any new listings from the Listing Manager
Collect agent requests from the intake form (one queue, no DMs)

weeklyRhythm.name: Produce
steps: Write captions, emails and GBP posts in one batch
Film 2 short videos with whichever agent is in the office (10 minutes each)

weeklyRhythm.name: Approve
steps: Review the approval queue in one sitting: approve, edit, or kill
The coordinator runs the compliance checklist before anything enters the queue

weeklyRhythm.name: Schedule
steps: Schedule social posts and GBP posts for the next 7 days
Load emails into Brivity with the right list segments

weeklyRhythm.name: Report
steps: Send a one-screen KPI snapshot to the CEO
Name 3 learnings and 1 change for next week
Ask 2 recent closings for a Google review

raci.activity: MLS entry and Clear Cooperation timing

listingLaunch.task: Listing agreement signed: create the launch card, book photos and video
Draft MLS remarks, flyer, social, email and texts from the launch kit template
Agent and seller approve copy; compliance checklist passed
Live on the MLS first. Public marketing follows within 1 business day (Clear Cooperation)
Just-listed post, GBP post, and story go live
Open-house email to buyer segments in Brivity
Open house; sign-ins captured with text consent
Seller marketing report: views, saves, showings, feedback

compliance: Brokerage line on every public asset (Evelo Team | Keller Williams Indy Metro NE)
Fair housing scan: describe the property, never the people
Every statistic names its source and period; list price is never called sale price
Emails: physical address and unsubscribe. Texts: opted-in only, STOP language
Testimonials are quoted exactly, with permission on file

kpis.name: Leads by source
kpis.definition: New contacts by lead source (social, GBP, website, Fello, referral, open house)

kpis.name: Appointments set
kpis.definition: Buyer and listing consults booked from marketing-sourced leads

kpis.name: Google Business Profile actions
kpis.definition: Calls, website clicks and direction requests

kpis.name: Social reach and saves
kpis.definition: Accounts reached; saves and shares per post (saves signal useful content)

kpis.name: Email engagement
kpis.definition: Click rate and replies by segment (opens are unreliable)

kpis.name: Review velocity
kpis.definition: New Google reviews per month (419 at 5.0 as of September 2026)

kpis.name: Listing launch on-time rate
kpis.definition: Share of new listings that hit every launch milestone on schedule

kpiNote: Targets are set after a 30-day baseline. Setting targets before measuring is guessing.
